law: A producer capability is promoted to supported-and-exposed product status only when the executable workbench covers it. Promotion is earned by executable playground/inspection coverage on the canonical exposure descriptors, not asserted by a producer's own claim.

preconditions.requirement: The capability has a DX1 exposure-descriptor registration (a DX0 feature-exposure-contract.v1 operation row, or its successor DX1 contract), with hostExecutionClass, answerRail, maturity and producing owner taken from the producing owner and the product-surface catalog, never from the consuming surface's presentation.

An executable workbench route exists: a runnable route in the playground workbench (or inspection surface) that a user can invoke without internal tooling, producing a source-linked result or explanation on the correct answer rail with its completeness state.

A replay scenario exists and is registered (DX6/DX6R-lineage replay case): re-running the route on the recorded receipt basis reproduces the recorded result; routes that cannot be replayed are not executable coverage.

Every route result binds the DX0 product-receipt-basis field set (sourceRevisions, projectConfiguration, engineIdentity, hostIdentity, completenessState) and rejects stale-basis results instead of publishing them.

rule.nativeOnlyClause: A NativeOnly capability is promoted only with real, explicitly selected native execution through the DX4/DX5 companion route (or a BWH1-admitted browser semantic host whose build proves the closure). An inactive/disabled card, an undocumented shell escape, arbitrary companion command execution, or a silently substituted Portable engine each fail the rule regardless of UI presence.
rule.futureClause: A capability whose producer does not ship anywhere yet is future: it registers as a named obligation with its producing node (PG0-AC2), renders as the distinct future/unsupported state, and stays out of promotion. Future framework/profile support (PG0.4) acquires these obligations automatically when its descriptors register; the workbench neither implements missing framework compilers nor replaces TypeScript.
rule.demotion: Removing an executable route, breaking its replay case, or unbinding its receipt basis demotes the capability back to promotion-blocked. Product superiority claims from installation or protocol smoke alone are forbidden; a protocol smoke or screenshot is not semantic-correctness proof.
enforcement: PG0-AC1: the discriminating join runs in tests/playground/PG0/pg0.test.mjs — every DX0 operation id maps to exactly one feature-matrix operationCoverage row with equality on hostExecutionClass, answerRail, browserExecutable, workbenchState and promotionBlocked; a promoted (exposed/unblocked) operation without its matrix row, route owner and obligations fails coverage.
PG0-AC2: a family row with familyState future must name its futureProducer and must not claim any exposed operation; a family presenting success without a shipping producer fails.
The promotion ledger itself is owned by the existing PM/ledger authority; this rule is the contract the ledger enforces, not a second status store.

ownership.producerAuthority: Semantic algorithms, project resolution, format/lint logic, TypeScript projection and edit transactions stay with their existing producing owners; promotion changes exposure status, never producer ownership.
ownership.retirement: The manually curated compiler-demo feature list (Output.vue allTabs) is retired by PG2's generated explorer cutover; between ratification and cutover the curated list is characterized and preserved, and after cutover two active feature-coverage authorities may not coexist.
